en: The Śrīhemakāmākṣī-daṇḍaka (The Hymn in Dandaka Meter to the Auspicious Hemakāmākṣī)
He bears a golden splendor shining within a halo of light whose essence is the syllable *Oṃ*;
with his right hand he holds a pet parrot whose sweet speech is the three Vedas, while his left hand holds a hanging staff;
beautiful in his triple-bent posture (*tribhaṅgi*), his feet bow down to those who are distressed and afflicted.
May that [form] which bestows auspiciousness through its side-glances and is magnificent with a gentle smile sport within my heart.
On her right side is Kāmajit, on her crest is Kāmavallabha, and beneath her garment is Kāmāyudha; I bow to that Kāmākṣī.
I bow to Kāmākṣī, whose forehead mark is Desire, whose son is the garland of desire,
and whose speech is like one blinded by desire.
I bow to that Goddess Gāṅgamātā, adorned with a garland of Gaṅgā flowers,
who has gone to the earth to protect mortals, her very body being the Gaṅgā.
Victory to you, O half-bodied consort of Ekāmreśvara! Victory to you, O playful one of Tañjāpurī!
Victory to you, O Kāmākṣī of Vaṅgāru! Victory to you, O bestower of all goals!

Victory to you, O Mother, who preside over Kāñcī—the foremost of most meritorious regions, served by the hosts of gods and asuras—in your own essential form; O wish-fulfilling gem for the granting of the desires of devotees! O Mother! Having fashioned a beautiful golden form in accordance with the splendor arising from the third eye of Mūladevī,
and having installed you in a certain place at Dhruva, the Lord of Vaṇīs, after performing a magnificent wedding festival in Kāñcī together with Ekāmranātha, [proceeded further].
O Kāmākṣī! I have always united you with this very King of the Sky (Ākāśabhūpāla) to perform your great festival.
By the crushing of the excellent seat Kāmakoṭī, the lotus-born Brahmā, whose vision was lost, performed the worship of the wheel and likewise propitiated you;
thus, through his well-executed practice, he regained the full light of his sight.
O Mother! When the army of the Karnaṭakas, brought into terror by the Yavanas,
was about to seize Śeñci, you were quickly reached by the foremost disciples of Durvāsas stationed at Varasthāna, and you became worshipped by King Santāna.
Then, having been propitiated for a long time by the lord of Uḍiyārpālaya,
you joyfully traveled through many villages and regions; thereafter, having spent very long years there,
you [resided] by the excellence of the fortune of the sovereign of Tañjāpur.
Having reached that holy city of Tanjore, and having obtained land granted by King Tūlajendra—
who was established there in this auspicious temple which shines with the interior of the Rāmakṛṣṇa shrine— those virtuous ones perform the worship prescribed by Durvāsas in the *Saubhāgyacintāmaṇi*.
Furthermore, that temple of yours, which possesses many portions increased by the Śarabha and Mahipa [lineages],
has been completely renovated with the expenditure of no small wealth by the eminent lords of the Kāñcīpīṭha and the foremost among the performers of religious duties.
O you who have the moon as your crest-jewel, who have surpassed the intoxicated swan through your excellent state, who have transcended the swan in luster, O you whose shoulders are bowed!
O Mother, on days graced by the asterism of Phalgunī during the months of Tulā and Mīna, perform here festivals such as the birth and marriage ceremonies;
and during the autumn, at nightfall, celebrate the principal festival with a divine consecration preceded by the most magnificent preparations.

They are the multitudes of devotees [who cry out]: "O root of eternal bliss! O you who delight in the noble elephant! O you whose teeth are as pure as jasmine buds! O auspicious one! O you who are thoroughly perfumed by the semen of the musk-deer! O you who are related to the husband of Jānakī! O you who were praised by the son of Jamadagni!"
O you who are praised by Madhura Sukavi Mūka! O you who are propitiated by the venerable Durvāsas! O you who are honored by Dhaumya and true devotees! O you who are served by Śaṅkarācārya!
O you who are worshipped by the lords of the Kāñcī-pīṭha! O you who are celebrated by the king of music, the renowned Śyāmaśāstrī!
O you who grant good fortune to those preceded by the recitation of that [mantra], I, a wretched person, always meditate upon you, the purifier.
O Mother, quickly cast upon me a glance thick with compassion;
grant me the pure purification of mind and the knowledge of the Self; forgive the offense committed by me against you, and bestow upon me eternal happiness both in this world and the next.
Bestow firm devotion upon Your lotus feet from afar;
salutations to You, O Śivā, grant me auspiciousness; protect me, O Kāmākṣī, protect me, O Kāmākṣī!
Oṃ tat sat.
